subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: Should this Codex native PreToolUse security fix require `code_mode_exec` normalization and packaged Codex runtime proof before merge, or should maintainers accept the current patched-runtime prerequisite and unified-exec/session tradeoffs as-is?
rationale: The remaining blocker is not just implementation mechanics: merging changes tool-execution enforcement, session reuse, and dependency expectations for policy-active Codex users, so maintainer intent is needed after the mechanical mapping repair.

options.title: Require mapping and runtime proof
options.body: Normalize `code_mode_exec` into the existing `exec` policy surface, refresh the branch, and require proof against the packaged Codex runtime before considering merge.

options.title: Accept current prerequisite
options.body: Maintainers may explicitly accept the local patched-runtime prerequisite and the unified-exec/fresh-thread compatibility changes, but that still leaves the mapping repair to make the security boundary coherent.

options.title: Pause behind another draft
options.body: Keep this draft paused while deciding whether the broader disablement or fail-closed related PR should own the security posture instead.

recommendation.title: Require mapping and runtime proof
recommendation.body: Normalize `code_mode_exec` into the existing `exec` policy surface, refresh the branch, and require proof against the packaged Codex runtime before considering merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and history put steipete closest to the current alias/docs surface and native hook fallback behavior that define the merge-risk decision.
